admin_search.title: Web search
admin_search.intro: A search backend answers {#code}POST /v1/search/\{backend\}{/code} — an authenticated, metering passthrough: the gateway counts the request, attaches the backend's own credential, and forwards the caller's body to the vendor verbatim, returning the vendor's answer verbatim (ADR 0071). Backends are absent from {#code}/v1/models{/code} unless a client asks for them explicitly, so no other client will mistake one for a chat model. Who may search is the grant below; how much they may search is a request ceiling on Quotas.
admin_search.state.none: none yet — add the first one
admin_search.grants_body: One grant per backend — creating the backend made its row. What the caller sends inside the body (a depth, a result count) is the vendor's own pricing, not a decision this screen makes.
admin_search.tiers_empty: No backends yet. Add one above.
admin_search.policy_heading: Which backend each group searches through
admin_search.policy_body: The policy behind {#code}POST /v1/search{/code} (no backend in the path): one request shape in, one answer shape out, through exactly this backend at its default depth. Only backends the group is granted above are offered — a group with none set cannot use the unified route at all.

admin_users.toggle.authelia_failed: The bundled login could not be updated
admin_users.toggle.disable_sessions: Their console session, chat sessions and machine links are refused within about a minute. Refresh credentials and minted API keys are revoked at once.
admin_users.toggle.disable_keys: Personal API keys are kept but stop admitting requests while the account is disabled — they return automatically if you re-enable it.
admin_users.toggle.disable_bundled: Their bundled Authelia login is disabled too, under the same action.
admin_users.toggle.disable_idp: This does not disable the person at the identity provider — do that there too, or they can still authenticate even though the gateway refuses them.
admin_users.toggle.enable_body: They can sign in again immediately, and personal API keys admit requests again. Sessions, minted keys and devices stay revoked — they sign in again and re-enroll rather than resuming automatically.
admin_users.toggle.enable_bundled: Their bundled Authelia login is re-enabled too, under the same action.

admin_routing.title: Routing
admin_routing.subtitle: Aliases — names your callers send that resolve to one or more models. Access is granted on the alias, billing follows the model that served the request.
admin_routing.caption: Model aliases
admin_routing.load_error.title: Could not load the aliases
admin_routing.reason.target_deleted: The model this alias pointed at was deleted. The name still exists and still has its grants, but nothing can serve it — point it at a model again.
admin_routing.reason.target_inactive: The model this alias points at is inactive. Activate it, or point the alias somewhere else.
admin_routing.reason.target_provider_ina: The provider behind the model this alias points at is inactive. Activate the provider, or point the alias somewhere else.
admin_routing.reason.target_is_alias: This alias points at another alias, which is refused. Point it at a model.
admin_routing.form.name: Name
admin_routing.form.name_hint: What callers send as {#code}model{/code}. Callers cannot tell an alias from a model.
admin_routing.form.display_name_hint: Optional. How this name appears in a model picker.
admin_routing.form.kind_hint: Taken from the targets. An alias can only point at models that serve the same API surfaces, so this cannot be changed here.
admin_routing.form.no_targets: No model to point at. Add a model first.
admin_routing.delete.title: Delete {name}
admin_routing.delete.body: Callers sending {#code}{name}{/code} will get “model not found” from the next request. Spend already recorded stays in the ledger.
model_detail.aliases.title: Aliases pointing here
model_detail.aliases.description: Retargeting or deleting this model changes what these names serve. They are removed from {#code}/v1/models{/code} and answer 503 until they point somewhere usable again.
model_detail.aliases.affected_note: They are not deleted with the model: each keeps its name and its grants, and can be pointed at a model again from the Routing tab.

admin_routing.rule.first_available_hint: Try the targets in the order listed; the first that is up and admitted serves.
admin_routing.rule.weighted_hint: Pick a target at random in proportion to its weight; the draw also sets the fallback order.
admin_routing.rule.cheapest_hint: Pick the target with the lowest list price (input plus output). A target with no price is tried last.
admin_routing.form.targets_hint: In order of preference. If a target fails for its own reasons (unreachable, timeout, 429, 5xx) or is not admitted by quota, the next one is tried, up to three in all. A streamed answer never switches target once it has started.
admin_routing.form.sticky_hint: A session that sends a session id stays on the target that served it for this long. 0 turns stickiness off.
